message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the **presence of a mane in adult male lions**. The mane is a secondary sexual characteristic that develops due to a dominant allele (or set of alleles) that influences the growth of dense, dark hair around the head and neck. While not all male lions develop a full mane—size, density, and coloration can vary—the underlying genetic mechanism that allows a mane to form is typically governed by dominant genes. This trait is often used as a visual cue for dominance, health, and reproductive fitness within lion prides.
